correctness.rationale: For every lattice L with λ1(L)≥5, no two different centers share a neighborhood triangle and an opposite horizontal pair has a unique common center: any two candidate lift differences would produce a nonzero period of Manhattan norm ≤4. Thus for each of N centers the displayed triangle/tetrahedron and then edge/triangle are free simplicial pairs, disjoint among centers, giving exactly 2N elementary collapses. Remaining two triangles per center are a translation quotient of the two planar diamond triangulations indexed by coordinate parity. The period lattice exchanges the planes iff some (a,b)∈L has odd a+b; each orbit quotient is an orientable flat 2-torus. f=(N,3N,2N), Betti (c,2c,c), c=1 or 2. This is an all-lattice universal-cover proof, not an extrapolation from finite verification; inspected checker independently implements actual pair deletions for 104 twisted grids.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge: Shukla (arXiv:1802.04526, Theorems 2.5–2.6, 4.4 and Lemma 4.2) already determines homotopy types and uses triangle collapses in various cyclic 4-regular circulant cases, so those cyclic overlaps and technique are credited. It does not cover arbitrary finite-index rank-two lattices with noncyclic quotient group, exact 2N collapse and parity/deck formula. Morris (arXiv:2301.05396) computes toroidal grid graph automorphisms and bipartiteness, not neighborhood PL cores. Matsushita computes group-theoretic π1 relationships without this explicit topological classification.
